item.title: Verifiable Settlement and Pricing for Local Energy Markets: Architecture and Deployment on Hyperledger Besu
item.description: arXiv:2611.16495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We implement privacy-preserving local electricity exchanges using an automated market maker on the Hyperledger Besu network under QBFT consensus. The proposed protocol operator collects individual electricity positions off-chain and publishes aggregate supply and demand on the blockchain, where smart contracts compute market prices every fifteen minutes. Individual positions remain off-chain; Poseidon2 commitments and UltraHonk zeroknowledge proofs, generated from Noir circuits, verify aggregation, payments, and daily balance updates. The architecture retains community coordination while making financial execution independently auditable. Signed receipts and member-triggered recourse prevent unverified or partial settlement. In a ten-household experiment using simulated US residential profiles, daily settlement uses approximately 19 million gas and produces eight-member proofs in 2.4 seconds. Over four simulated days, local trading covers 34.4% of demand and reduces grid-only costs by 30.5% under assumed tariffs. Numerically computed __-Nash Equilibrium electricity profiles capture 83-88% of the social planner surplus.
item.dc:creator: Michele Fabi (CREST), Baptiste Leloup (ENSAE)

item.title: Improving Algorithmic Trading for BESS on Intraday Electricity Markets through Distributional Price Forecasts
item.description: arXiv:2611.17170v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) are becoming increasingly important in short-term energy markets, where they help balance fluctuations in variable renewable generation. In many countries, the continuous intraday market is the most important wholesale market for BESS to monetize their flexibility. In this paper, we propose an extension to the myopic rolling intrinsic policy that incorporates intraday price forecasts tailored specifically to the BESS trading problem. While a large literature addresses intraday price forecasting, most existing work focuses on volume-weighted prices during the last hours of trading and consequently fails to capture the features most relevant to BESS trading. Our approach addresses this gap by introducing a novel target variable derived from the limit order book and its dynamics. The resulting forecasts are designed to inform the optimization about future profit opportunities while preserving computational efficiency and avoiding the burden of full stochastic optimization. In a realistic high-frequency simulation setting covering 2023 and 2024, our method improves profits by up to 42% over the naive rolling intrinsic formulation. We further analyze the relationship between forecast accuracy, stability, and financial performance, establishing a clear inverse relationship between accuracy and stability. Finally, we find evidence that BESS size and duration jointly influence both overall profitability and the marginal benefit of incorporating forecasts.
item.dc:creator: Simon Hirsch, David Schaurecker, David Wozabal

item.title: TradeMech: A Method to Multilaterally Net Trades Without Altering Counterparty Exposure
item.description: arXiv:2605.15210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Financial markets such as bond, derivatives, and repo markets form networks of interdependent obligations. Existing multilateral netting methods typically trade off the extent of netting against preservation of counterparty exposure: central clearing reallocates exposure to a central counterparty, while trade compression may alter bilateral counterparty relationships. TradeMech is a mechanism for markets in which one or two homogeneous fungible objects are traded. The mechanism transforms a network of initial bilateral contracts into chains and cycles, nets the designated object multilaterally on those chains and cycles, and replaces initial contracts with multiparty contracts whose assigned trades remain fractions of the original bilateral trades. The construction achieves maximal multilateral netting of the designated object while preserving each agent's contractual profit and preserving the location of counterparty risk. When a party fails to pre-commit a required object, the affected assigned trade is recovered as a bilateral contract between the same original counterparties and the remaining assigned trades are re-netted on residual chains, so no new counterparty exposure is created.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Aronoff, Robert M. Townsend, Madars Virza

item.title: Deep Learning of Robust Market Making under Regime-Switching Order Flow
item.description: arXiv:2609.11614v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical market-making strategies based on stochastic control, such as the Avellaneda--Stoikov and the Gu\'{e}ant--Lehalle--Fernandez-Tapia (GLFT) extension, provide closed-form quoting approximations, but rest on assumptions that break down at realistic microstructure timescales. One of them is that order flow is stationary, while empirical evidence points to the existence of regimes, possibly associated with algorithmic execution of metaorders. In our experiments, persistent directional flow makes stationary controllers unprofitable. In this paper, we develop a deep reinforcement-learning market maker (RLMM)---a Rainbow-style distributional deep Q-network which is calibrated and tested in a zero-intelligence limit order book. We find that, in the stationary setting, RLMM outperforms GLFT at comparable levels of profit and loss (PnL) dispersion. The stationarily trained RLMM is more robust to flow asymmetry than GLFT, but still suffers inventory saturation and large drawdowns under persistent directional flow. Training a separate RLMM under regime-switching flow, with a Bayesian flow-belief signal and a queue-adjusted quote exposure signal, restores positive mean PnL in our experiments. A final scenario-bandit step prioritizes low-return scenarios and improves performance under varying regime persistence and directional correlation.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Moret, Fabrizio Lillo

item.title: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain
item.description: arXiv:2611.13616v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On blockchain-based exchanges, faster blocks weaken the priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Equilibrium liquidity peaks at an interior block speed; beyond a threshold, an active liquidity provider cream-skims and passive capital shrinks. Evidence from the Base Flashblocks upgrade, a tenfold block-speed increase, confirms the predictions. Priority-fee bids decrease sharply and arbitrageurs' net profit rises. The active liquidity provider rebalances faster, avoids toxic flow, and earns a higher profit. Pool depth falls and effective spreads widen despite closer tracking of external prices.
item.dc:creator: Ruizhe Jia, Shihao Yu

item.title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.12537v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a trader executes a large order, the relevant question is not \emph{what will the price be?} but \emph{what would the price have been had I not traded?} Market impact is thus a causal quantity, yet classical models (Almgren--Chriss, propagators) regress price on flow, which is biased whenever informed flow moves prices through information as well as trading. We present a proof-of-concept \emph{Causal Market Simulator}: a continuous-time causal prior-data fitted network (PFN) trained on a synthetic market prior in which a hidden informational flow confounds the flow--price relation by construction, with confounding strength an exact per-episode knob. On this prior, the naive estimator's bias follows a closed form we confirm empirically (up to 68\% overestimation), while the PFN tracks the unbiased true-parameter oracle at high confounding. Its \emph{do-ablated twin}, the same model with the intervention inputs removed, collapses onto the pre-window mean. Zero-shot, the model responds at the ground-truth scale to metaorders in an ABIDES limit-order book (+0.38 pre-onset standard deviations against seed-replay counterfactuals), and its intervention response replicates on about 2,300 detected flow bursts in BTC/ETH/SOL perpetuals and 3,800 on Nasdaq equities, evidence consistent with, though not proof of, causal transfer. Off-prior the response degrades gracefully, and split-conformal recalibration repairs interval calibration. Transfer hinges on encoding the metaorder as added flow rather than a clamped price level, not on more training. A recurrent state-space variant closes the remaining shape gap: its impact accrues over execution duration where the transformer's stays flat, raising the correlation with measured metaorder impact from +0.68 to between +0.92 and +0.96, at the cost of weaker on-prior deconfounding that traces to the training recipe rather than to recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Thumm, Ying Chen
